title: Arrays
story: Bash has arrays. They hold lists without the word-splitting bugs of plain strings.
goal: Put the arguments into an array, then print the count, the first item and the last item on separate lines, then every item in reverse.

tests.label: four
tests.expect:
4
a
d
d
c
b
a

tests.label: spaces
tests.expect:
2
x y
z
z
x y

hints: ${#items[@]} is the length, ${items[0]} is the first item.
Count down with for ((i=len-1; i>=0; i--)).

items=("$@")
echo "${#items[@]}"
echo "${items[0]}"
echo "${items[-1]}"
for ((i=${#items[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
  echo "${items[i]}"
done
socratic: Why is ("$@") safer than a string?
How do you get the last item?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Arrays”?
solution:
items=("$@")
echo "${#items[@]}"
echo "${items[0]}"
echo "${items[-1]}"
for ((i=${#items[@]}-1; i>=0; i--)); do
  echo "${items[i]}"
done
alt:
items=("$@")
echo ${#items[@]}
echo "${items[0]}"
echo "${items[${#items[@]}-1]}"
for (( i=${#items[@]}; i>0; i-- )); do echo "${items[i-1]}"; done
